title: Check List & Test Report for Fire Intercom & PWD Intercom
source: spec/Fire_and_PWD_Intercom_Test_Report.html — a one-page sheet: a document block, a three-item readiness checklist ticked YES / N/A / NO, a zone table where each zone heading carries a Call Function and a Fault Condition result, and a three-column sign-off. The supplied file was saved with a completed record in it (Apple AMK 2&3 Level 1; PWD Zone 1 and Fire Intercom Zones 67, 68, 72, 73, 74); those are record values, not template values, and are not carried here — including the SYSTEM field's "P&S", which is left blank for the engineer rather than carried as a default that may not be right for the next panel.

sections.title: Readiness Checks
sections._note:
`page_break_before` on the opening section is what keeps this on one sheet: `paginate` gives every section its own page unless at least one declares a break, and a break on the first section is a no-op for layout — it is already page 1. Same idiom as `fcu-lcp-checklist.json`.

The source's eight document fields are the record header rather than a section of their own: they are one grid on the paper, directly under the banner, and the header info block prints them the same way without spending a section heading on them.

The three readiness items are the paper's, verbatim. `status` rather than `pass_fail_na` so the choices read YES / N/A / NO in the sheet's own order and wording; the outcomes make a "No" derivable as an outstanding item (SPEC §6). The paper has no remarks column against these items — the renderer always prints one, so it is labelled and left for whatever the engineer needs to qualify a N/A with.

rows.description: Control panel is ready to test
Battery back-up is ready to test
Zone number labeled on site and provided at the control panel

sections.title: Zone Tests
sections._note:
**One row per zone, where the paper spends three.** The source writes a zone heading — "1. PWD Zone 1", "2. Fire Intercom Zone 67" — and hangs two bulleted sub-items beneath it, Call Function and Fault Condition, each with its own Passed / Failed / N/A dropdown. The two sub-items are the same for every zone, so they are columns, and a zone becomes a single row. That prints the same information in a third of the height and, more to the point, lets a panel with twenty zones be one record.

The zone name is record data and typed per row — the source makes it an editable field for the same reason (Hard Rule #5). Numbering comes from `auto_number`, which is what the source's own "1.", "2.", "3." prefixes are.

**Why this section starts page 2.** Measured on the live build: a page gives 877px to content, a zone row costs 35px, and the document block, readiness table, zone table and sign-off together come to 924px even with the table at its minimum three rows — 59px past A4, which prints as a second sheet while the footer still reads "Page 1 of 1". One sheet holds only a single-zone record, and this form exists for panels with many (six on the source sample). Breaking here gives 347px on page 1 and 660px on page 2 at six zones, with room for about twelve before page 2 needs its own break.

This is also what replaces the source's "+ Add page" button: that clones the whole sheet, header and sign-off included, purely to get more zone rows. Here the table grows and the record stays one document with one sign-off.

sections.title: Sign-off
sections._note:
An in-flow `sign_off` section rather than the top-level `footer`: PrintView always gives the footer a page of its own, which would print a one-page source on two sheets. Both routes carry the same slots through `collectSignatureSlots`, so the status workflow is unchanged. Same idiom as `ductwork-air-leakage-test.json`.

The source's three columns, and it heads the lower two identically — "WITNESS BY" — so the roles read the same here; the distinct `stage` values are what drive the workflow (SPEC §6), as on `sensor-calibration-record.json`.

The paper's sign block carries only Name, Signature and Date — no company column. The renderer always prints Company, so Performed By defaults to Kenyon Pte Ltd and stays editable (unlocked, as on `staircase-pressurization.json`); the two witness companies are left blank for whoever attends.
